title: Hindu College staff and students protest in Delhi over admissions and governance
seoTitle: Delhi Hindu College protest over admissions

tea.why: Staff and students are protesting against alleged admission irregularities, financial opacity, and governance issues at Hindu College.
tea.want: Protesters demand an independent probe into admissions, transparency, an inquiry into commercial use of resources, and university takeover.
tea.changed: Nov 4: TRS founder and president K Kavitha joined the protesting students and staff to express solidarity.

summary: Teaching and non-teaching staff and students of Hindu College in Delhi have been agitating for over a month against alleged irregularities in admissions under Sports and Extra-Curricular Categories, financial matters, and the commercial naming of college spaces after corporate donors. The Hindu College Staff Association has sought an independent investigation into admissions and called for Delhi University to take over the college to prevent privatisation. The President's Secretariat forwarded a staff complaint to the Union Ministry of Education after Lok Sabha MP Sudhakar Singh visited the protesting teachers. Delhi University attributed the admission discrepancy to a technical error in its centralised admission algorithm, while Hindu College Principal Professor Anju Srivastava rejected the allegations, stating admissions are handled centrally.
demands: Independent probe into alleged irregularities in admissions
Inquiry into financial and procurement irregularities
Investigation into commercial use and renaming of college buildings
Delhi University takeover of the college with an extended governing body
response: Delhi University attributed admission discrepancies to a technical error in its centralised algorithm and denied deliberate violations. Principal Anju Srivastava rejected allegations, stating admissions are conducted centrally. The President's Secretariat forwarded a staff complaint to the Union Ministry of Education.

updates.text: Lok Sabha MP Sudhakar Singh visited the protesting teachers and later raised the matter with the President.
TRS founder and president K Kavitha joined the ongoing protest to extend solidarity with the students and staff.
